body.x: Teaching robots to handle objects with the dexterity of a human hand depends on high-quality data showing how people actually do it, and complex manipulation tasks are slow to develop and hard to scale without that data.
What if that data could be captured directly from people wearing a hand exoskeleton and reused across robots?

Q&Q, a deep-tech company based in Greece and operating as Haptikos, is led by CEO Greg Agriopoulos and works on human-machine interaction, haptics, physical AI and robotics. At KES 2026, Haptikos is presenting its platform and benchmark results and running live demonstrations and user testing, with the aim of finding Korean early adopters.

Its wearable hand exoskeleton and software platform capture human demonstrations and translate them into data for training robots. The company describes this as a data infrastructure layer for automating high-dexterity tasks, and says the core of its differentiation lies in the sensors and algorithms inside the device. According to the company, Haptikos data improved efficiency in NVIDIA global benchmarks, and it is part of NVIDIA's Inception program for startups.

Haptikos reports more than 40 customers, including robot makers Agile Robots of Germany, GBionics of Italy and TETRA Dynamics of the United States, along with robot training organizations and corporations. It has raised USD 3.5 million and run more than 30 pilots in Europe. The company has exhibited at NVIDIA GTC 2026, AWE USA 2025, MIT Reality Hack, TNW and Nagoya Messe.

Haptikos currently sells in Europe and the United States, where it is in early sales and works directly with a limited number of lead customers. South Korea, Japan and China are the next markets because of their robotics and physical AI ecosystems. The company is seeking three kinds of partners: robot builders such as humanoid OEMs and dexterous-hand makers, platform providers such as simulator and teleoperation vendors, and large Industry 4.0 corporations automating dexterous tasks on existing robot arms.

It plans to raise a USD 7.5 million seed round to reach a fully commercial-ready solution and expand its team. Local partnerships, partner matching and verification programs, and support for overseas exhibitions are what it says would help most in entering new markets.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
